description: Three shapes of connection escape - returned from the function, stored into a table field, handed to a helper that does not close it - each leave `conn` in a non-final connection state at function exit with no reachable transition to `closed` anywhere in the function, and are expected to produce effect.lifecycle.unreleased at the acquisition site. The message/evidence shape mirrors declared-resource-lifecycle's single-path-leak template (2 evidence rows: acquisition, then missing-proof-at-exit; e.g. its leak_on_pcall_error_path case) rather than its 3-row partial-close template, because none of these three functions contains any resource.close call on any path. There is no separate declared wording for 'escaped' versus 'merely left open': the manifest's own doc comment (internal/testfixture/standard_target.go, resourceHostManifest) and the coverage census (GAP-015: PublicationEffectCloseRelease/PublicationLifetimeRelease are undeclared vocabulary anywhere in this manifest) confirm nothing marks return/store/pass-through as a release of ownership, so a returned or stored handle is exactly as unreleased as one dropped on the floor under the CURRENT declared surface. The fourth function, passes_to_closing_function, hands the connection to a helper that itself calls resource.close on it - ownership moves into the callee and is released there - and is the negative control: zero diagnostics, proving a real (interprocedural) close is still recognized as reaching the final state.
